title: Machine learning-enabled identification of nucleus pulposus senescence-associated genes as potential biomarkers for intervertebral disc degeneration
summary: Analysis of the GSE70362 gene-expression data identified TAF13 as a candidate nucleus-pulposus senescence-associated marker for intervertebral disc degeneration. Random forest and SVM recursive feature elimination contributed to the selection; qPCR and Western blot in vivo assays, followed by qPCR in human nucleus-pulposus tissue, supported the reported expression pattern. Clinical diagnostic performance or utility was not demonstrated.
ai_technology: Random forest and SVM recursive feature elimination with co-expression analysis
organization: Department of Orthopedics, Affiliated Hospital of Guangdong Medical University, Zhanjiang, 524000 China; Collage of Integrated Traditional Chinese and Western Medicine, Southwest Medical University, Luzhou, 646000 Sichuan China; School of Medicine, Putian University, Putian, 351100 Fujian China

evidence.tested: The study analyzed expression profiles and used qPCR and Western blot in vivo, plus qPCR in human nucleus-pulposus samples, to assess TAF13 expression. These assays supported the marker’s expression pattern in the reported material.
evidence.unknown: The biomarker claim is not a demonstration of clinical diagnostic performance or utility in an independent prospective patient cohort; expression associations do not establish causality.
evidence.ai_role: Random forest and SVM-RFE prioritized genes associated with disc degeneration; subsequent assays examined the selected TAF13 expression signal.

source_review.scope: Primary result-bearing material for the stated method, result and evaluation, with bibliographic version information.
